note: DeadTimer has no component of its own. The shared Quantum TimerComponent serves both SwitchTimer and DeadTimer; the actor type picks the behaviour. The full address-by-address derivation lives in the module header comment; this file records the conclusions, the verification and what it unlocks.
summary: A DeadTimer counts down and, at zero, broadcasts QEventType.Dead(19) to every actor in the scene. It does not read m_TargetName, it never collides, and it kills nobody directly: each receiver decides. Players die unless they are immortal. Slots 15..18 encode a mercy rule that lengthens the timer once the party has failed the stage repeatedly.

typeDispatch.evidence: TimerComponent.ParseParameter 0x18172dd1b..0x18172dd47 writes a word for the actor type: 0x0a (DeadTimer) -> 0x102, 0x1f -> 0x101, 0x25 (SwitchTimer) -> 0x103.
typeDispatch.meaning: Low byte is m_TimeUpType, high byte m_Type. A DeadTimer is therefore always TimerTimeUpType.Dead(2) + TimerType.TimeDown(1).
typeDispatch.dispatch: onTimeUp 0x18172e070 branches on m_TimeUpType at 0x18172e0ba..0x18172e0ce: Retry(1) 0x18172e203, Dead(2) 0x18172e132, Switch(3) 0x18172e0d0.

timeUpSequence: 0x18172e132: GetEventParam(QEventType.Dead = 19) then Frame.NotifyEvent 0x181749790, the param-only overload, which walks the whole ActorScene list (0x181749a10..0x181749af2) and invokes OnRecvEvent on every actor. m_TargetName is never consulted: this is a stage-wide broadcast.
0x18172e1a4: FrameEvents.PlaySe 0x18174bd50 with SeId 2 (Blip), volume and pitch raw 0x10000.
0x18172e1cf: btr [stage+4],9 clears StageComponent m_Flags bit9, i.e. SetEnableOpenWindow(false) (owner 0x181709ca0).
0x18172e03a sets m_Flags bit3 afterwards, so a time-up fires at most once per attempt.

whoDies.evidence: PlayerComponent.OnRecvEvent 0x1816c1187 -> 0x1816c174e handles event 19: return if m_Life <= 0 (0x1816c174e jle); return if param.CauseDead != Fall and IsImmortal (0x1816c1758 cmp [param+0x6c],1 then 0x1816c1773 test [p+0x20],0x100); otherwise m_Life = 0 (0x1816c1789) and m_RequestedPlayerState = QPlayerState.Dead(3) (0x1816c17a2).
whoDies.consequence: QEventParamManager.Get zeroes the param, so CauseDead is Contact(0) and the immortal test does apply. An immortal player survives a DeadTimer.

mercyRule.where: DeadTimer-only block in ParseParameter 0x18172da97..0x18172dcea, guarded by cmp dword[createParam+0x30],0xa so a SwitchTimer never enters it.
mercyRule.selector: datas[15] is floor()ed and compared with 1 at 0x18172dadb. Only the exact value 1 enables the block; it also supplies the first table index via lea r8d,[rax+0xf] = 16 at 0x18172daeb.
mercyRule.tables: datas[16], datas[18], datas[17] are read in that order as QPlayerCountParam<int> (DeserializeInt 0x180970770) and resolved for the live population by QPlayerCountParamUtility.Find 0x181786950.
mercyRule.arithmetic: 0x18172dbee..0x18172dc13: A = Find(datas[16]); skip if A <= 0; n = Frame.GetGameOverCount 0x1817475d0; skip if A > n; B = Find(datas[18]); C = Find(datas[17]); skip with a log at 0x18172dc60 if B <= 0 or C <= 0; else m_Sec += min((n - A + 1) * C, B).
mercyRule.order: The bonus is applied AFTER the datas[6..12] population override, so an override does not erase it.
mercyRule.shippedValues: Every world DeadTimer authors A=5 ('&'), C=2 ('#'), B=10 ('+') except st_w_13_02 which authors A=9 ('*'). Nothing happens until the party has failed five times, then +2s per further failure, capped at +10s.
mercyRule.counterSource: StageComponent.CountGameOver 0x18170dd60 increments it, guarded by m_Flags bit15 (IsCountedGameOver 0x181709cc0) so it rises at most once per attempt.

notASolid: TimerComponent has no InitCollision and no OnCollided, so solids() is always empty for both timer types. A DeadTimer kills by broadcast, never by contact.

observations: datas[0] reads 10 but the population override table raises m_Sec to 15 for every count 2..8.
Time-up lands at exactly tick 900 (15.00s at 60Hz).
deadPlayerIds covers every player; an immortal player is excluded.
The emitted event is {broadcast:true, event:19, causeDead:0}; notices carry (TimeUp, Move, isWait false) and stageFlags carry enableOpenWindow false.
Bonus: 15s at gameOverCount 0..4, 17s at 5, 19s at 6, 25s at 9 and above (capped).
Setting datas[15] to 2 skips the block entirely and leaves 15s even at gameOverCount 20.

unlocks.closest: st_w_05_02 now needs no further device, only a widening of the spring/switch direction guard in spring-switch-runtime.js.

unresolved: TimerTimeUpType.Retry(1) at 0x18172e203 sets StageComponent m_Flags bit10 (RequestRetry 0x181709cf0). No shipped actor type reaches it, so the module throws rather than guessing.
Frame.DeltaTime's FP raw value is still unread (get_DeltaTime 0x18173a090 forwards a session field), so a tick count may differ by one from the original. Same gap the other ports record.

The m_Flags bit NAMES are not in the metadata: the bitfield is the shared 16 bit QFlags instantiation. bits 0..3 are named from behaviour, with the reading and writing addresses given in the module header.
Receivers other than PlayerComponent also answer event 19 (nine component types). Only the player path is modelled, which is what matters for the stages in scope.
